title: Cadence of Hyrule
subtitle: Hyrule moves to another beat
summary: Cadence of Hyrule is Brace Yourself Games' rhythmic adventure, released for Switch on 13 June 2019.
body: Cadence of Hyrule is Brace Yourself Games' rhythmic adventure, released for Switch on 13 June 2019. It combines Crypt of the NecroDancer's movement and combat with The Legend of Zelda's characters, places and music. Link, Zelda and Cadence explore a changing arrangement of Hyrule while acting to the beat. The familiar task of approaching an enemy gains a musical clock: the next direction must make sense both as a position on the map and as an action within the rhythm.

When enemies are present, movement and attacks follow the music. Maintaining that beat brings rewards, while learning an opponent's pattern helps determine which step will be safe next. Weapons, digging tools and recognizable Zelda items extend the possibilities. The overworld's regions are rearranged for each save, while some dungeons are generated again on a return visit. Exploration therefore combines landmarks with uncertainty, asking the player to read a new local arrangement even when the larger purpose of reaching the next temple is clear.

Danny Baranowsky's arrangements connect the rhythmic system to Zelda's musical identity. Diamonds persist after defeat and help support another attempt, while temporary items and rupees can be lost. Sheikah Stones provide return points and fast travel. A fixed-beat option removes the requirement to follow the soundtrack, and a second player can join cooperatively. The crossover gives the music an unusually direct job: recognizable themes establish the place while their pulse also determines the immediate timing of moving through it.
story_headings: Read the enemy and follow the music
A crossover carried by familiar melodies
